text:
Alex: Heads-up — I want to start a small design thread: slab coalescing vs copy-on-write for prefix cache memory reclamation. Can we discuss the correctness tradeoffs and an experiment plan?
Maria: Nice, we haven't had a focused convo on this. Short TL;DR of what I mean: coalescing merges adjacent cold slabs to reduce fragmentation; COW clones a slab on mutation so readers don't block writers.
Devon: My concern w/ coalescing is the window where ownership moves — we risk serving slightly stale KV pages unless we do a synchronous handoff. That could blow tail latency for hot reads.
Priya: COW increases peak memory but gives a deterministic read path (no global quiesce). For multi-tenant workloads COW avoids cross-tenant read anomalies if we make clone visible only after commit.
Alex: Agreed. I sketched three constraints we care about: 1) read-after-write correctness within prefix (no stale reads exposed), 2) bounded tail latency for hot prefixes, 3) overall memory overhead cap (we can't double mem under sustained churn). Thoughts?
Maria: Could we do hybrid: COW for hot prefixes (tracked by hotset counter) and coalescing for cold slabs during background compaction? That limits COW peak.
Devon: Hybrid might work. But implement complexity spikes: need robust hotness heuristics + safe demotion path from COW -> coalesced representation.
Priya: Implementation sketch: annotate slabs with a small state enum: {Shared, COWing, Coalescing, Immutable}. Writers set COWing and clone; readers check state and use clone pointer if present. Async background coalescer only operates on Immutable slabs.
Alex: That helps correctness but how to avoid races where coalescer thinks adjacent slabs are cold when a writer just started a COW? We need an epoch or lightweight generation counter.
Maria: We already have a lease epoch for prefix ownership — reuse it. Coalescer only merges slabs whose epoch <= global_closed_epoch. Writers bump slab epoch on COW.
Devon: Practical question: how do we measure memory overhead and performance before landing? I propose a sandbox workload that simulates skewed tenant churn (10k tenants, 1% hot, synthetic mutate/read mix). infra-bot can spin up a small cluster with mem/cpu limits.
infra-bot: To run the sandbox: `./tools/sandbox-run --profile=evict-slab-coalesce-vs-cow --tenants=10000 --hot=100 --rps=2000 --mutate=0.2`
Priya: Add instrumentation we need: per-slab alloc size, clone count, epoch transitions, staleness incidents (read observed older value than last write), and 99/999 latency per prefix. Also track GC pause times for coalescer.
Maria: For correctness validation add a deterministic shadow client that issues sequence numbers per prefix and asserts monotonicity on reads (can detect stale reads). That'll catch read-after-write bugs.
Alex: Good. For performance we should sample token-level latency but also compute tail-latency distribution by tenant. Hot tenants are the real hazard.
Devon: One more tradeoff: coalescing can actually lower memory drastically for churny workloads if fragmentation is the dominant waste. In some runs COW overhead is unacceptable. We should record RSS and heap fragmentation.
Priya: Operational fail-safe: if memory exceeds a configured threshold, force-enable synchronous coalescing reclaim on least-recently-used cold slabs (blocking reclaim). That avoids OOM at cost of spikes but is safe fallback.
Maria: Implementation checklist (short): 
- infra feature: sandbox profile + dataset generator (Devon)
- runtime: slab state enum + atomic pointer to clone (Priya)
- coalescer: epoch check and backoff (Alex)
- monitoring: metrics and shadow-client assertions (Maria)
Devon: I'll own the sandbox harness and initial perf runs. Expect first data by EOD Friday.
Alex: I'll draft a short RFC follow-up with the hybrid pattern and state machine. Put a note to include rollback plan (config flags to disable COW or coalescer independently).
Priya: Can we keep the API surface zero for users? i.e., internal-only toggles via runtime flags — no schema changes to prefix API.
Maria: Yes, that's cleaner. Also add a deprecation path if we find coalescing unsafe for certain customers (dedicated deployments might prefer predictability).
Devon: Quick note on tests: add unit test to assert readers see latest committed value when writer finishes (use in-memory epoch bump). Also add chaos test that kills background coalescer mid-merge.
Alex: Awesome. Any blockers?
Maria: Only one: need infra quota to run sandbox cluster at scale. Devon said he'll request it.
infra-bot: Quota request created: ticket RI-8421.
Alex: Cool. If no objections I'll start the RFC doc and tag folks. :thumbsup:
Priya: :thumbsup:
Devon: :+1:
Maria: Thanks — looking forward to results.
